I am Dr. Agent. You mentioned fatigue, flank pain, and fever following recent antibiotic treatment for sinusitis; can you tell me exactly when your symptoms started and which antibiotics you took?

speaker: Patient
text: I have been feeling tired, feverish, and I have flank pain. These symptoms continued even after my sinus symptoms improved.

speaker: Patient
text: I was first treated with amoxicillin for sinusitis and developed a rash. Then the antibiotic was changed to cephalexin for another week, and the rash went away. A doctor I saw earlier said this was very likely Pyelonephritis and told me the presentation was already quite typical.

speaker: Doctor
text: The medication change to cephalexin after a rash suggests an allergy to amoxicillin, but the fact that the rash resolved makes a drug reaction less likely. Did you experience chills, nausea, or any changes in your urine color or frequency since starting the second antibiotic?

speaker: Patient
text: I do not have nausea, vomiting, or burning with urination. I also have not noticed a major change in urine color.

speaker: Doctor
text:
Since you lack urinary symptoms like dysuria or frequency, and your urine color is normal, I am concerned this might be an extra-urinary complication rather than a standard infection. Did you experience any localized pain or swelling in your kidney area, or do you have any skin rashes or joint pain?

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Systemic Lupus Erythematosus (SLE) presenting as acute lupus nephritis with secondary pyelonephritis.

Although the initial presentation of fever and flank pain after antibiotic treatment mimics pyelonephritis, the negative ANA, normal complement levels, and the absence of typical urinary symptoms make a primary autoimmune etiology with renal involvement the leading diagnosis, potentially complicated by a superimposed infection.
